title: Distributed logistics · mission sequence
subtitle: 2024 TTX · dispersed basing and logistics constraints
description: Logistics evidence from Mitchell Institute's 2024 CCA tabletop exercise: disperse CCA, preposition stocks, compare kinetic vs electronic attack sortie planning, and assess theater-airlift risks (pp. 24–25, Figure 12).
assumptions: The study analyzed potential force postures and logistics; it did not publish actual transport tracks, replenishment schedules, basing access agreements or sortie outcomes.
Southern Japan/Ryukyus and northern Philippines were broad forward areas considered by teams, not exact coordinates of approved launch sites.
The constrained-logistics sortie shares in Figure 12 are percentages from TTX team plans, not observed combat statistics.
Current animated paths, timing and individual actors are editorial illustrations only.

phases.title: Preposition forward stores
phases.narrative: The teams favored prepositioned replacement CCA and munitions because wartime resupply of forward sites could be high-risk.

phases.title: Distributed CCA posture
phases.narrative: Road- and rocket-launchable notional variants reduced reliance on airfields in southern Japan and the northern Philippines.

phases.title: Generate CCA sorties
phases.narrative: Low-footprint support concepts are examined alongside projected shortages of air-to-air munitions.

phases.title: Theater airlift risk
phases.narrative: Teams identified high risk for crewed C-130 replenishment near contested operating areas and examined uninhabited cargo options.

phases.title: Shift to non-kinetic effects
phases.narrative: With constrained logistics, the sweep team's weapon-launch share fell from 96% to 68%; the SEAD team's fell from 76% to 33% (Figure 12).

phases.title: Sustain under attack
phases.narrative: The report emphasizes fuel, local support, munitions commonality and resilient dispersed operations rather than an exact basing plan.
